column1: This most common of emotions is turning out to be more interesting than we thought
column2: 这种再平常不过的情绪，正显出比我们想象中更有意思的一面。
column3: most common of emotions|最常见的情绪
column4: turning out to be|结果发现是
column6: than we thought|比我们原先以为的

column1: We all know how it feels — it’s impossible to keep your mind on anything, time stretches out, and all the things you could do seem equally unlikely to make you feel better.
column2: 我们都知道无聊是什么滋味：注意力落不到任何事情上，时间仿佛被拉长，想到能做的种种事情，又觉得哪一件都不太可能让自己好受一些。
column3: keep your mind on|把注意力放在……上

column1: But defining boredom so that it can be studied in the lab has proved difficult.
column2: 不过，要把无聊定义得足够清楚，使它能够在实验室里被研究，并不是件容易的事。

column1: For a start, it can include a lot of other mental states, such as frustration, apathy, depression and indifference.
column2: 首先，无聊可以包括许多其他心理状态，如挫败、冷淡、抑郁和漠不关心。

column1: There isn’t even agreement over whether boredom is always a low-energy, flat kind of emotion or whether feeling agitated and restless counts as boredom, too.
column2: 无聊是否总是一种无精打采、平淡低沉的情绪，焦躁不安、坐立不宁又能不能算无聊，连这一点人们都还没有共识。

column1: In his book, Boredom: A Lively History, Peter Toohey at the University of Calgary, Canada, compares it to disgust — an emotion that motivates us to stay away from certain situations.
column2: 加拿大卡尔加里大学的彼得·图希在《无聊：一段生动的历史》中，把无聊比作厌恶。厌恶是一种促使我们远离某些情境的情绪。
column3: Boredom: A Lively History|《无聊：一段生动的历史》

column1: ‘If disgust protects humans from infection, boredom may protect them from “infectious” social situations,’ he suggests.
column2: “如果说厌恶能保护人免受感染，那么无聊或许也能让人远离具有‘传染性’的社交情境。”他推测道。

column1: By asking people about their experiences of boredom, Thomas Goetz and his team at the University of Konstanz in Germany have recently identified five distinct types: indifferent, calibrating, searching, reactant and apathetic.
column2: 德国康斯坦茨大学的托马斯·格茨和同事们询问人们感到无聊时有何体验，最近辨认出五种不同的无聊：淡然型、调适型、寻求型、抗拒型和麻木型。
column3: experiences of boredom|感到无聊的体验

column1: These can be plotted on two axes — one running left to right, which measures low to high arousal, and the other from top to bottom, which measures how positive or negative the feeling is.
column2: 这五种类型可以标在两条坐标轴上：横轴从左到右表示由低到高的心理唤醒程度，纵轴从上到下则表示这种感受偏积极还是偏消极，以及程度如何。

column1: Intriguingly, Goetz has found that while people experience all kinds of boredom, they tend to specialise in one.
column2: 有意思的是，格茨发现，人们虽然会体验各种无聊，往往却以其中某一种为主。
column7: specialise in one|在其中一种上表现尤为明显

column1: Of the five types, the most damaging is ‘reactant’ boredom with its explosive combination of high arousal and negative emotion.
column2: 五种类型中，危害最大的是“抗拒型”无聊：高唤醒程度与消极情绪结合在一起，一触即发。

column1: The most useful is what Goetz calls ‘indifferent’ boredom: someone isn’t engaged in anything satisfying but still feels relaxed and calm.
column2: 最有益的则是格茨所说的“淡然型”无聊：当事人没在做什么能带来满足感的事，却仍觉得放松、平静。

column1: However, it remains to be seen whether there are any character traits that predict the kind of boredom each of us might be prone to.
column2: 不过，是否有某些性格特征能够预测我们每个人更容易体验哪种无聊，还有待观察。
column3: remains to be seen|还有待观察

column1: Psychologist Sandi Mann at the University of Central Lancashire, UK, goes further.
column2: 英国中央兰开夏大学的心理学家桑迪·曼把看法又推进了一步。
column4: University of Central Lancashire|中央兰开夏大学
column5: goes further|提出更进一步的看法

column1: ‘All emotions are there for a reason, including boredom,’ she says.
column2: “所有情绪的存在都有原因，无聊也不例外。”她说。

column1: Mann has found that being bored makes us more creative.
column2: 曼发现，无聊会让人更有创造力。

column1: ‘We’re all afraid of being bored but in actual fact it can lead to all kinds of amazing things,’ she says.
column2: “我们都怕无聊，但它其实能带来种种令人惊喜的事。”她说。

column1: In experiments published last year, Mann found that people who had been made to feel bored by copying numbers out of the phone book for 15 minutes came up with more creative ideas about how to use a polystyrene cup than a control group.
column2: 曼在去年发表的实验研究中，让一组人抄写电话簿里的号码15分钟，令他们感到无聊。她发现，随后让大家设想聚苯乙烯杯子能用来做什么时，这组人想出的点子比对照组更有创意。

column1: Mann concluded that a passive, boring activity is best for creativity because it allows the mind to wander.
column2: 曼得出的结论是，被动而单调的活动最有利于发挥创造力，因为它能让思绪自由游走。
column7: the mind to wander|让思绪自由游走

column1: In fact, she goes so far as to suggest that we should seek out more boredom in our lives.
column2: 事实上，她甚至建议，我们应该在生活中主动为自己多找些无聊的时刻。
column4: goes so far as to|甚至提出要
column6: in our lives|在我们的生活中

column1: Psychologist John Eastwood at York University in Toronto, Canada, isn’t convinced.
column2: 加拿大多伦多约克大学的心理学家约翰·伊斯特伍德并不认同。

column1: ‘If you are in a state of mind-wandering you are not bored,’ he says.
column2: “如果你的思绪正在漫游，你就不是在感到无聊。”他说。
column3: in a state of|处于……状态

column1: ‘In my view, by definition boredom is an undesirable state.’
column2: “依我看，按定义，无聊是一种令人不快的状态。”
column5: undesirable|adj. 不受欢迎的，令人不快的

column1: That doesn’t necessarily mean that it isn’t adaptive, he adds.
column2: 但他补充说，这未必意味着无聊没有适应功能。

column1: ‘Pain is adaptive — if we didn’t have physical pain, bad things would happen to us.
column2: “疼痛就有适应功能。如果我们感受不到身体疼痛，就会有糟糕的事发生在我们身上。
column3: Pain is adaptive|疼痛具有适应功能
column5: would happen to us|就会发生在我们身上

column1: Does that mean that we should actively cause pain?
column2: 这是否意味着我们应该主动制造疼痛？

column1: No.
column2: 当然不是。

column1: But even if boredom has evolved to help us survive, it can still be toxic if allowed to fester.’
column2: 同样，即便无聊是在进化中形成、用来帮助我们生存的，如果任其积久恶化，也仍然可能有害。”
column7: if allowed to fester|如果任其积久恶化

column1: For Eastwood, the central feature of boredom is a failure to put our ‘attention system’ into gear.
column2: 在伊斯特伍德看来，无聊的核心特征是我们未能启动自己的“注意系统”。

column1: This causes an inability to focus on anything, which makes time seem to go painfully slowly.
column2: 这样一来，我们便无法专注于任何事情，只觉得时间过得慢得令人难受。
column5: makes time seem|让人觉得时间

column1: What’s more, your efforts to improve the situation can end up making you feel worse.
column2: 更糟的是，努力改善处境，到头来反而可能让自己感觉更不好。

column1: ‘People try to connect with the world and if they are not successful there’s that frustration and irritability,’ he says.
column2: “人们想和外部世界产生联系，一旦做不到，就会感到挫败和烦躁。”他说。

column1: Perhaps most worryingly, says Eastwood, repeatedly failing to engage attention can lead to a state where we don’t know what to do any more, and no longer care.
column2: 伊斯特伍德说，也许最令人担忧的是，反复集中不了注意力，可能使我们陷入一种既不知道还能做什么，也不再在乎的状态。

column1: Eastwood’s team is now trying to explore why the attention system fails.
column2: 伊斯特伍德的团队正试图弄清，注意系统为什么会失灵。

column1: It’s early days but they think that at least some of it comes down to personality.
column2: 研究还处在初期，但他们认为，原因至少有一部分归结于个人性格。
column5: comes down to|归根结底在于

column1: Boredom proneness has been linked with a variety of traits.
column2: 研究发现，容易感到无聊的倾向与多种特质有关。
column3: Boredom proneness|容易感到无聊的倾向

column1: People who are motivated by pleasure seem to suffer particularly badly.
column2: 那些行事主要受追求快乐驱使的人，似乎尤其容易深受无聊之苦。

column1: Other personality traits, such as curiosity, are associated with a high boredom threshold.
column2: 另一些性格特征，比方说好奇心，则与较高的无聊阈值相关，这类人不容易感到无聊。
column6: high boredom threshold|不易感到无聊的高阈值

column1: More evidence that boredom has detrimental effects comes from studies of people who are more or less prone to boredom.
column2: 对不同程度上容易感到无聊的人所作的研究，也为无聊的有害影响提供了更多证据。
column6: more or less prone to|或多或少容易……

column1: It seems those who bore easily face poorer prospects in education, their career and even life in general.
column2: 那些容易感到无聊的人，似乎在教育、职业生涯乃至整体生活中都面临较差的前景。

column1: But of course, boredom itself cannot kill — it’s the things we do to deal with it that may put us in danger.
column2: 不过，无聊本身当然不会要人性命。可能让我们陷入危险的，是我们为了摆脱无聊而做的事。
column6: put us in danger|使我们陷入危险

column1: What can we do to alleviate it before it comes to that?
column2: 那么，在事情发展到这个地步之前，我们能怎样缓解无聊呢？
column5: comes to that|发展到那个地步

column1: Goetz’s group has one suggestion.
column2: 格茨的研究小组有一条建议。

column1: Working with teenagers, they found that those who ‘approach’ a boring situation — in other words, see that it’s boring and get stuck in anyway — report less boredom than those who try to avoid it by using snacks, TV or social media for distraction.
column2: 他们对青少年的研究发现，有些人选择“直面”无聊的处境，也就是即便觉察到事情枯燥，仍会投入进去。与那些靠吃零食、看电视或刷社交媒体来分心逃避的人相比，他们自述感到的无聊要少一些。
column7: report less boredom|自述较少感到无聊
column10: distraction|n. 分散注意力的手段

column1: Psychologist Francoise Wemelsfelder speculates that our over-connected lifestyles might even be a new source of boredom.
column2: 心理学家弗朗索瓦丝·韦梅尔斯费尔德推测，我们这种与外界联系过密的生活方式，甚至可能成为无聊的新来源。
column4: over-connected lifestyles|与外界过度连接的生活方式

column1: ‘In modern human society there is a lot of overstimulation but still a lot of problems finding meaning,’ she says.
column2: “现代社会给人的刺激已经太多，但人们要从中找到意义，仍然困难重重。”她说。
column3: modern human society|现代人类社会

column1: So instead of seeking yet more mental stimulation, perhaps we should leave our phones alone, and use boredom to motivate us to engage with the world in a more meaningful way.
column2: 所以，也许我们该暂时放下手机，借无聊推动自己以更有意义的方式与世界发生联系，而非继续寻求更多的精神刺激。
column5: leave our phones alone|暂时不碰手机
column7: engage with the world|与世界发生联系
